question.text: A put writer receives Rs. 40 premium for a put with strike Rs. 900. Stock closes at Rs. 870. What is the P/L?

explanation.text: The Logic: Short Put P/L = Premium - max(X - S, 0). With Premium = 40, X = 900, S = 870: payoff to the buyer = max(900 - 870, 0) = Rs. 30. The Rs. 30 payoff is less than the Rs. 40 premium received, so the writer still earns Rs. 10. Stated differently, spot 870 is above the writer's BEP of X - P = 860. The Trap: Loss of Rs. 30 mistakes the buyer's payoff for the writer's loss and ignores the premium. Loss of Rs. 10 reverses the sign. Profit of Rs. 40 ignores the buyer's payoff and assumes the writer keeps the full premium. Note: Broken fragment after "payoff (30)" repaired — explanation now reads "payoff of Rs. 30 is less than the Rs. 40 premium received, so the writer still earns Rs. 10."
